title: Transformation of Energy
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 8 Integrated Science; not yet checked by a CBC Integrated Science teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Demonstrations: a pendulum (potential to kinetic), a torch (chemical to electrical to light), a solar toy, a bicycle dynamo, rubbing hands (kinetic to heat). The child writes each change as an arrow chain. Energy safety covers electrical, heat and moving parts.

skills.key_step: The child names forms of energy (heat, light, sound, electrical, chemical, kinetic, potential) in real objects and sorts sources into renewable (sun, wind, flowing water, geothermal, biomass) and non-renewable (coal, petroleum, natural gas).

floor.prerequisite: Knows sources of electricity in Kenya.
floor.question: Name one source of electricity in Kenya.

representations: objects: a ball, a torch, food, a stretched catapult
a map of Kenyan power sources
steps: Moving: kinetic. Raised or stretched: potential.
Stored in food and fuel: chemical.
Renewable: replaced by nature. Non-renewable: will run out.

board.do: Write coal, sun, petrol, wind, geothermal.
Ask the child to sort the rest.

misconceptions.ask: How long does coal take to form?
Does the sun rise every day?

listen_for: a rolling ball has chemical energy

misconceptions.ask: What lets you run after lunch?

checks.question: Is petroleum a renewable or non-renewable source?
What form of energy does a stretched catapult have?

skills.key_step: The child writes the energy changes in a device or event as a chain (a torch: chemical to electrical to light and heat), says energy is not created or used up but changes form, and names safety measures.

floor.question: What form of energy does a moving ball have?

steps: Follow each part of the device.
Note wasted heat; energy is never lost, only changed.

board.do: Draw a torch: cell, wire, bulb.
Ask the child to write the rest of the chain.

misconceptions.ask: What does the kettle do to the water?
misconceptions.repair: A kettle changes electrical energy to heat.

misconceptions.ask: Where did the energy of the falling stone go?
misconceptions.repair: Energy changes form; it is not lost.

misconceptions.ask: What does the panel send down the wire?
misconceptions.repair: A solar panel changes light into electrical energy.

misconceptions.ask: What carries the energy from the cell to the bulb?
misconceptions.repair: Write each step of the chain.

checks.question: Write the energy changes in a solar lamp at night.
checks.answer: light to electrical (charging by day), then chemical in the battery, then electrical to light

checks.question: What happens to energy when a ball stops rolling?
checks.answer: it changes into heat (and some sound); it is not lost
